direct_or_reviewed.confidence_boundary: Catalog binding / bounded lexical evidence / reviewed effect scope are retained separately; execution is unverified.

contract.review_scope: Body-level static contract; transitive application and called-module completeness are separate.
contract.purpose: Clear group and assignment from the selected system-directed process subset.
inputs_defaults: groupNumber nvarchar(50), processStamp nvarchar(100), userStamp nvarchar(30), dateTimeStamp datetime; no defaults.
null_and_invalid_input_behavior: NULL/empty group takes no branch. Stamp arguments are used as supplied; dateTimeStamp targets a nonnullable column and NULL can fail the statement.
output_shape: No SELECT result set or explicit result code.

ordered_branches.explanation: Update matching group rows restricted to one internal process code: clear GROUP_NUM, USER_ASSIGNED and TEAM_ASSIGNED; write supplied process/user/time stamps.

contract.status_and_quantity_effects: Clears group/user/team assignment and replaces audit stamps; does not alter SEQUENCE, work condition or quantity.
configuration_scope_and_precedence: No feature/profile lookup, warehouse predicate or user-authorization validation in this body.
error_and_return_handling: No explicit error/return contract; UPDATE errors propagate.
contract.transaction_ownership: No explicit transaction, commit, rollback, savepoint, TRY/CATCH or XACT_ABORT is introduced by this body; caller/session semantics remain authoritative.
concurrency: One UPDATE statement is atomic under engine statement semantics; caller-level assignment conflict protection is not present here.
contract.trigger_behavior: Observed active-table trigger is AFTER INSERT, not this UPDATE.
external_handoffs_and_gaps: Which application path calls it and which internal process code is intended need caller reconciliation; a group number alone is not proof of authorization.

evidence.description: Complete module body reviewed with original-definition fingerprint.

global_limits: All claims are snapshot-scoped static evidence or explicitly labeled vendor behavior. No database/application operational execution.
A full body review with gaps is not whole-process semantic closure or runtime acceptance.
Code-family names never establish vendor/custom ownership.

limitations: This is the retained 2026-09-29 replica capture, not a new database inspection. The .sql file is the complete captured sys.sql_modules.definition encoded as UTF-8, including original comments, literals and line endings; nothing is prepended or reformatted. Captured definition text is not a complete deployment script: permissions, SET options, session context and dependencies are separate. No routine was executed. Static references do not establish branch execution, current use or runtime table scans. Vendor-base versus customer customization ownership is not established by names or comments.
A captured source reference establishes a static relationship, not that a module ran, a branch was reached, or a table is currently active.

NO_CAPTURED_REFERENCE means none of the credited channels in this exact retained corpus identified the table. It does not establish that the table is unused, obsolete, a backup, safe to delete, or absent from external application SQL.
Dynamic SQL, runtime-selected identifiers, external callers, client-generated SQL, uncaptured jobs and historical/other database code can use tables without a resolvable reference here.

The bounded lexer recognizes named SQL relation/DML positions and local aliases/CTEs; it is not the SQL Server binder. Unqualified names assume a unique captured name, not verified caller/default-schema resolution. Unsupported or ambiguous syntax remains explicit.

DDL, DBCC, permission statements and metadata-function arguments are not comprehensively classified by the parser. Their table relationships depend on captured catalog dependencies or reviewed effects; unmatched identifiers/string arguments remain non-credit observations.
Identifier tokens and string-contained names are separate non-credit observations. Column names and configuration text can match table names; neither proves an executed table access.
Foreign keys are structural relationships and never count as procedure/function usage. View paths are catalog/source paths; attached trigger paths are possibilities, not proof the event fired.
Owner backup/leftover and item-master-failure suggestions are hypotheses. Name patterns and missing references do not validate them. No deletion recommendation is made.
Current replica status is owner-attested. This task documents the captured source as-is and requires no application version/build or extension development.
All claims are snapshot-scoped static evidence or explicitly labeled vendor behavior. No database/application operational execution.
A full body review with gaps is not whole-process semantic closure or runtime acceptance.
Code-family names never establish vendor/custom ownership.
